text: i set a birthday reminder for my close friend for Sunday April 19th. the app was set correctly to sound an alarm at 6am. the alarm didn't actually go off until Monday 2 pm! what the hell?! thankfully I was able to remember myself. no it's not cause by aggressive power saving as the app has power usage priority. the problem is caused by buggy programming and poor app development/Dev support
author: Chris Vydas
developer_reply: Hi Chris, missing or delayed notifications are most commonly caused by aggressive power saving added by phone manufactures. As you will see online Motorola are notorious for this. Check out the help https://mytasksapp.com/help/faqs and here: https://dontkillmyapp.com/ If you need more help, just email me. I hope this helps your understanding, Steve

text: This is the best reminder app you'll use hands down. Two tricks I've picked up over years of using the app #1 Be sure in the settings on your phone to allow task app to operate even if yer phone is on Do Not Disturb mode. #2 Always have yer volumes including media, call volume, ring volume & alarm volume ON. Even if they are all on low volume, the app alarm will sound. Having one or more of these volumes off makes the task app glitch & won't work properly. Volumes ON = perfect running app.

text: GREAT app generally but minor flaw with repeated tasks. The entire system only refreshes at midnight so if you have a task at 11pm but don't complete it till 00:15 then you'll not get a reminder the next day, as it won't reset till the next midnight. Similarly if you want to (e.g.) take a tablet at 8am and 8pm (repeat every 12 hours), you'll not get the 8pm reminder because it's not yet refreshed the first. [emailed dev, got quick response and a work around, thank you.]

text: Being an advocate for efficiency in task management (and someone who has subscribed to GTD for many years), I am pleased to say that I am able to fit "Tasks" wonderfully into my work flow. I've used most apps out there (incl. macOS, PalmOS, cue cards and even file folders) and I've definitely run the gamut for this type of thing. I will give you some of my sagely advice, lol. ;) Here are some suggestions on how to incorporate Tasks into your own work flow; this is how *I* use it so feel free to do your own thing with this app and be creative!. Firstly, I use Task's "Lists" as "workspaces" or "domains" ("Home", "Work", etc.). What about contexts you say, well, I use Tasks' "Sub Lists" for those ("Waiting For", Someday", etc.). I deal with a lot of projects in my day-to-day; here comes tag support! Here is how I do it: I create tags (or codenames) for every project I am working on. After this is done, I I create a "List" called "Projects". I will from now on put *all* of my project tasks in there. This sounds crazy, I know, but hear me out. Using this method, whenever you add a task for a project, be sure to assign that project's tag to it. Now, using Tasks' other great feature -- "Smart Lists" -- create a Smart List -- one that only shows you that tag. Do this for each of your projects. When you are done with them, file them away in a new "List" (I call it "Workspace") called "Projects Archive" or something. There you go -- you now have project support. If you are using Tasks for projects in the manner like I am, you will have to buy it, but at that point, this app pays for itself itself. It really is quite remarkable. Smart Lists are also amazing. I have one Smart List called "Today + 1" which shows me stuff that is due over the next two days, and another one called "Next 60 Days" which shows me ONLY those tasks that have a due date and that are upcoming up in the next 60 days. This is all customizable, of course. Use your imagination. Speaking of customization, there are custom colors, you can add emoji's to your lists like I do, etc. Just go nuts. The most efficient people in the world can adopt almost any system into a powerhouse, but this application makes it too easy! One more thing I would like to add... Tasks allows for quick capture through either the Home Screen icon or Quick Settings menu. Those of you that have random tasks being thrown your way throughout your day will now how powerful this is. Avoid "Brain Drain" as David Allen calls it. I do want to add that this is the LONGEST review I have ever written in my life. I do admit that I am somewhat of an organization nerd, so there's that, but I also feel that this developer deserves recognition. I truly feel that this app stands above most others. Definitely an extremely strong contender as the best Task Management application, for sure. Kudo's to the developer for a job well done. Buy this one, guys, it's a gem, and it's worth it.

developer_reply: Wow! Just wow! Thank you so much for taking the time to send me your incredible feedback and support. Tasks is constantly growing and it is so nice to hear that all the features are so well received and used. Great organisational system, I shall be adopting some of your suggestions. Cheers, Steve

text: I have tried so many task tracking apps because all of them seem to be missing some critical feature, and this one is about as perfect as it gets! Love the lists and sublists, subtasks, notes, and flexible reminder repeat options (seriously, so many apps make this a paid subscription option). The only problem I have with it is the kind of odd way that it handles completing repeating tasks, and I'm hoping this is something that can be slightly altered to make this app perfect! There's two main problems: 1 - When you mark the task as complete, it stays marked as complete until the next time it goes off. You can "un-complete" it and it will appear as a pending task with the next time that it will go off, but this tends to have weird results sometimes. There is an option to "track history of repeating tasks," which duplicates the task when it's marked completed so there's a copy that will repeat and a copy that will go into the task history, but the duplicated task is also marked complete--leading to the same problem as mentioned above. 2 - You can tell the app to either set a completed task to repeat the specified amount of time from when it was completed (option A), or from when it went off (option B). (e.g., if my task that repeats once a week was due at 12pm Friday, but I don't mark it complete until 11am Saturday, Option A will have it repeat the next Saturday, and Option B will have it repeat the next Friday.) It's nice to have this option, but it would be way better if we could set it on a task-by-task basis. For me personally, I have a medication I take every two weeks; sometimes I take it late, and ideally, I should take it again exactly two weeks from then, so I would prefer option A for this one. However, I also have a reminder to back up my PC every Sunday; if I complete this late, I would still prefer option B and be reminded on Sunday every time, because that's when I generally have time to do it. I can only pick one style or the other, so I have it set to option B and just manually alter the ones that need it. It works, but it would be nice to have the option to automate it! Thanks for a great app and sorry for the super long explanation!

text: This app has a lot going for it: intuitive, customizable, with some well-designed features (e.g. sub-lists). Unfortunately, after buying a year's subscription, I found it largely unusable. There are bugs and missing features that don't allow for a reliable experience. First of all, although the developer claimed the web app was exactly like the phone app, it turns out that yes, it's virtually a carbon copy (which looks a bit odd on a large screen), but unfortunately it doesn't support some features, e.g. repeating tasks: you cannot add them, and for those that you created on the phone, only the first occurrence shows, but after it's completed, it no longer shows up, ever. So now I have WAY more items on my phone than on my laptop/PC, and the PC app is basically useless. And even on the phone, it doesn't quite work right, despite the developer's claims to the contrary. I've used dozens, if not hundreds, of todo apps, and the natural and obvious behaviour is that when you miss a daily repeating task, it shows up (in red or otherwise highlighted) on the next day, and when you tick it off, it reappears for the current day, because though you forgot yesterday, you want to be able to do it today. Not in this app. Here the task just disappears for today, basically setting you up to miss it again. It will only reappear the following day. So if you've missed a task, you'd better tick it off on the same day. Bizarre. Anyway, I'm switching to another app, which seems to be fully developed and so far behaves normally (though it might miss some of the cool features of this one). Maybe I'll come back to this one if/when it's completed.
author: Paweł Cisło
developer_reply: Paweł, the web app is still in beta. You will have seen and agreed to a consent dialog when you first opened the web app. Reminders require some server side prerequisites before they will work as users expect. Sorry, but writing software takes time and sometimes we have to be patient. If you had suggestions, you could have simply emailed me. Steve

text: I've been using this app successfully for over a year and could echo many of the things other users have written here (the ADD thing definitely rings a bell!). I chose this app after reviewing about a dozen other task manager apps on Google Play and have not been disappointed. I've been as impressed by the developer as by the app. He is rapid in responding to user issues, open to feedback, and has kindly made enhancements based on my specific suggestions. There is an amazing level of flexibility in this app while remaining pure in concept and simple to use. All this for free! But the Premium features are both affordable and amazing. The developer has somehow managed to deliver a web user interface identical -- in function, look and feel -- to the Android app. With one's task database safely stored in the Cloud, one can access it simultaneously via web and/or any of one's Android devices I give this app, in both its Android and web form, my highest recommendation!

text: AMAZING & SIMPLE APP for busy moms (& dads, & teenagers) or of course any one needing a little help to stay on top of their day, week, month - well you get my point! I do so many things outside of the usual grocery, things to do, people to call lists etc. The option to custom color code the list let me create one for each child (& husband!). I have coordinated my color code to the one for my calendar to help me keep everyone else's on track as well- as most moms do! It has options to create not only lists of items & tasks to do but also to track smaller tasks. I can even cross them off as I complete them. Such as planning ahead for upcoming celebrations like BIRTHDAYS for family & friends, a camping trip, my anniversary etc. This year I won't forget anyone! The sub task option can be used to divide different tasks my children are responsible like their chores i.e.Clean Kitchen> daughter cleaning up sub tasks vs. son's cleaning up sub tasks I can easily separate who will empty dishwasher, take down garbage bag, set dinner table and so on. It's perfect for preparing for back to school. I have short term task lists for back to school clothing needs, reminders to wash uniforms, days to pack lunches, sign permission slips, buy specific school supplies etc. I tried MANY "to do" apps and they either took too long to figure out how to use the fancy but unnecessary functions, that I ended up not even using or took too long to add an item to one of my lists as it pops into my head- they just weren't as user friendly as this app! This is a must have for everyone, not just moms, but great for teachers lesson planning, gardening crop sowing & harvesting, contractors' project planning even babysitting jobs! So happy I found it, and less stressed!

text: Formerly had complained about high battery usage until developer alerted me that there is a setting under Settings, that is called "Keep Screen On", which is enabled by default. As such, the app remains screen on continuously which causes battery drain. I would suggest having this setting "off" by default, or perhaps having some selectable intervals of 1,2 or 3 minutes. Otherwise, I really love this app, as it allows you to make infinite child lists of child lists, something you cannot do at all with Google Tasks. I had been looking for an app that allows me subtasks and this fits the bill as I could not find any other app as versatile and written such that a programmer could understand easily.
author: A Google user
developer_reply: Hi Phil, there is a setting "keep screen on" which you simply need to disable. You could have done me the courtesy of emailing me to ask. Tasks is a hobby project of mine and many users wanted the screen to remain on when walking around the supermarket etc. I hope this helps, Steve

text: Beautifully designed app. Simplistic in its design yet powerful in its flexibility. Really loved the fact that I could create multiple lists and then filtered lists (today's list, today's high priority list, today's office list etc.) I could find almost all features I was looking for. Color coding for lists works great for people who like it visual. Settings is pretty awesome, giving amazing customization - I personally loved the font resizing (cozy) setting because it showed me the complete task description and full day view on screen without scrolling. One minor issue I found is - recurring tasks don't show in all days. I set up a recurring task for Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. When I check the calendar view for the week, that task is shown on Monday only (not sure if it will come up on Wednesday's task list once Monday's task is completed). Please get this issue fixed - a recurring task should be visible on all days. Another minor wishlist is - if we can set a due date without being forced to choose a time. Overall a great app!

developer_reply: Hi Vasuki, thank you for your fantastic feedback. If the time is optional, would you still want a notification? If yes, when would you expect to see it? Thanks, Steve

text: 9/12/19 morning: I use this app constantly and love it to pieces. It so nicely keeps me organized in all the different aspects of my life and in one central place. It's simple, easy to use, and very effective. The only thing i haven't figured out how to do yet is back it up. If my phone melts down, i lose my lists, or if I get a new phone. Probably this my ignorance just not knowing yet how to do the backup correctly. Thanks for an awesome app. 9/12/19 afternoon: Ok, so Steve, the creator of this app, responded immediately to my comments about backup and showed me exactly how best to do it. You simply take any list you want to back up and go to the "Share" icon at the top right hand corner of the list window. Click on Share and then send yourself an email of the list. It comes through perfectly, super simple and fast. Lots of lists don't need back up because they are just "To Do" lists of various kinds, but other Lists like "Things to Remember," "Information to Keep," "Travel Information," "Family Facts," etc. are really important to back up especially as time goes by and they build up in content. I am very happy with this solution. Thanks Steve!.

text: Compared to the competition this is a very good todo app. It does the basics the best. The reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is that it does not seem to have a way to sync with a desktop or web application.   One thing that doesn't work well in my day to day life, in any to-do app, is more customizable sorting. Either it's too manual, making the todo app more of an interruption, or the sorting doesn't predict my priorities well. The simplest solution would be to combine basic sorting (priority, due date, category, etc) with manual sorting somehow. One way would be to have items initially sorted by your selected method. Then allow the user to manually sort any item. When a new item is placed in a list  the new item would be placed in order according to the those items that have not been manually sorted. If all items in the list have already been manually sorted then there are two approaches I can think of. Either have new items automatically be placed at the top or bottom in those cases, or even better the app could have hidden values for this. e.g. an item due 2/16 that's manually moved ahead of an item due 2/12 would be considered having a "due date" of 2/11 for sorting.

Sync and web app have been very popular suggestion and so I am currently working on server code to enable device to device sync, cloud backup and list sharing. "Tasks" has those two features and many more:  *Add items with minimal keystrokes.  *Configure whether new items get added to the top or bottom of the list.  *Quickly move an item within a list.  *Nested lists (with two list levels, anyway.)  *Easy backup to a local file.  And on top of all that, the app looks really nice.  A few suggestions for the developer, although these would be merely icing on the cake:  1. Add a black theme for OLED screens.  2. Remember which sub-task list is selected within each list when I switch between lists.  3. Provide an option to move an entire sub-task list from one list to another.  All in all, a big thank you to Mr. Nottage!
